title: Kenton Grua: Grand Canyon Legend
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck profile Kenton Grua, a Grand Canyon river guide and dory pilot known for his 1980s speed runs down the Colorado River and his 1970s thru-hike of the entire Grand Canyon. The episode covers his early life in Vernal, Utah, his work with Martin Litton's Grand Canyon Dories, the history of Colorado River expeditions from John Wesley Powell onward, the 1983 flood-year record run in the Emerald Mile with Rudy Petschek and Steve Reynolds (including the overturn at Crystal Rapid and the unpermitted night run), and his death in 2002. The episode ends with a listener mail about remembering port and starboard.

segments.title: Opening banter and writer welcome
segments.summary: Opening banter, welcome to new writer Anna Green, and a note that the Kenton Grua topic was thought to be a listener suggestion.

segments.title: Grand Canyon visits and the book The Emerald Mile
segments.summary: Hosts discuss visiting the Grand Canyon, recommend Kevin Fedarco's book The Emerald Mile and the documentary Into the Canyon, and talk about hiking out of the canyon.

segments.title: Kenton Grua's early life and first river trips
segments.summary: Grua was born in Salt Lake City in 1950, moved to Vernal, Utah at twelve, and began solo rafting on the Yampa River with an army surplus raft.

segments.title: Hatch River job and Martin Litton
segments.summary: Grua left plans for mechanical engineering to work for Hatch River Expeditions, quickly became a guide, then worked for Grand Canyon Expeditions where he met mentor Martin Litton, a conservationist.

segments.title: Dory boats and Grand Canyon Dories
segments.summary: The history of the wooden dory, its origins as a sea fishing boat, and why Litton used dories on the Colorado; Grua piloted the Chattahoochee for Grand Canyon Dories for about ten years and nearly 100 trips.

segments.title: Commercialization of Grand Canyon trips
segments.summary: Hosts discuss how modern Grand Canyon trips are commercialized and easier than early expeditions, and mention the proposed development on the canyon plateau.

segments.title: Grua's personality and habits
segments.summary: Grua's nickname was The Factor; he was known for drinking, cannabis use, unconventional clothing, and being opinionated but kind to passengers.

segments.title: Colin Fletcher and the Grand Canyon hike
segments.summary: Grua read Colin Fletcher's book The Man Who Walked Through Time and decided to hike the entire Grand Canyon, not just the national park portion.
topics: The Man Who Walked Through Time

segments.title: First failed hike and successful 1978 thru-hike
segments.summary: Grua's first attempt failed after moccasins wore out and a cactus cut his foot. He returned four years later with work boots and supply caches and completed roughly 600 miles in 36 days.

segments.title: Colorado River expedition history
segments.summary: Hosts describe the 1869 John Wesley Powell expedition, the three members who left on foot and died, and the Colorado River's significance.

segments.title: Motorboat and speed record attempts
segments.summary: Ed Hudson set a motorboat record in 1949; Jim and Bob Riggs broke it in 1951 by rowing; the longest trip took 103 days in 1973.

segments.title: Glen Canyon Dam and the tamed Colorado
segments.summary: Grua arrived after Glen Canyon Dam was built; the river had been wild before flood control, and river gradient and canyon steepness are discussed.

segments.title: Grua's 1980 speed record
segments.summary: Grua set a speed record in 1980 of 46 hours 56 minutes, beating the Riggs record, but wanted to go faster.

segments.title: 1983 El Niño flood conditions
segments.summary: El Niño snow caused extreme flows in June 1983 of 70,000 to 100,000 cubic feet per second, changing the rapids and overwhelming Glen Canyon Dam operators.

segments.title: Planning the Emerald Mile run without a permit
segments.summary: Grua, Rudy Petschek and Steve Reynolds planned the run; the Park Service denied a permit, and Martin Litton's call to the superintendent produced no answer, so they launched.

segments.title: River movie tangents
segments.summary: Hosts digress on the movie River Wild and Benjamin Bratt's Alcatraz birth fact.

segments.title: Launch just before midnight
segments.summary: The crew launched just before midnight on June 25, 1983 and paddled in total darkness, feeling the oars for obstacles.

segments.title: Roaring Twenties rapids and eddy fences
segments.summary: The crew faced the Roaring Twenties rapids and eddy fences at night, taking rapids without scouting.

segments.title: Crystal Rapid and ranger encounter
segments.summary: At Crystal Rapid, park ranger Benjamin Bratt was stationed to stop unpermitted boats after a commercial boat capsized and a passenger died earlier that day; the ranger, a former guide, pretended not to see them.

segments.title: Overturn at Crystal Rapid and continuing
segments.summary: The Emerald Mile overturned at a huge wave in Crystal Rapid; Reynolds was injured and the two others rowed on in extreme heat.

segments.title: Sleep stop and final push to record
segments.summary: The crew slept three hours, then resumed with extra oars and finished in 36 hours 38 minutes, breaking Grua's previous record.

segments.title: Aftermath, death, and legacy
segments.summary: Grua kept his guide license after a fine and community service; he died in 2002 at 52 while mountain biking, and founded the Grand Canyon River Guides; his dory company was sold to Oars.

segments.title: Closing remarks on Grua's death and dory tours
segments.summary: Hosts joke about his death and dory tours being too long for them.

segments.title: Listener mail: port and starboard mnemonic
segments.summary: A listener shares his grandmother's mnemonic 'there's not much port left in the glass' for port versus starboard, and hosts discuss their own memory tricks.
